speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to begin our assessment, how long have these symptoms been present, and were they sudden in onset or did they develop gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor) causing Pancoast Syndrome, likely secondary to underlying malignancy given the weight loss, smoking history, and progressive right arm weakness/sensory loss. I will now request imaging to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray, Chest_CT.
